handoff.reason: RCT found MORE radiation enteritis with glutamine 30 g/d than placebo (55.9% vs 22.0%, P=.002) -- a signal against benefit/possible harm in this indication, worth safety-review attention.

Pivotal SCD trial: low-grade nausea, noncardiac chest pain, fatigue, and musculoskeletal pain occurred more frequently in the l-glutamine group than placebo; glutamine also only tolerated in about two-thirds of patients per 32309821.
Review explicitly pools oral AND parenteral glutamine studies together without separating results by route; flagged for anyone reusing its pooled estimates as oral-specific evidence.

identity_notes: L-glutamine's retrieval set is dominated by two large confounds: (1) a huge body of PARENTERAL/ENTERAL critical-care and perioperative nutrition literature (TPN, alanyl-glutamine dipeptide infusions, dialysis-fluid additives, feeding-tube formulas) that is NOT evidence for oral supplement use and was rejected not_this_route throughout, and (2) a large cluster of neuroscience/metabolomics false matches where 'glutamine'/'glutamate' appears only as a measured neurotransmitter or biomarker (brain MRS studies in schizophrenia, Alzheimer's, autism, psychosis; metabolomics panels in diabetes, cancer, glaucoma, etc.), rejected off_topic or not_intervention. Among genuine oral trials, the strongest, most consistent single-ingredient efficacy signal is in sickle cell disease (pivotal Phase 3 trial 30021096, supporting FDA approval as Endari, corroborated by real-world data 35979207 and reviews 32309821/42628795) -- though tolerability was limited to about two-thirds of patients and adverse events (nausea, chest pain, fatigue, musculoskeletal pain) were more frequent than placebo. A second reasonably clean body of oral-glutamine evidence exists for GI/mucosal indications (postinfectious IBS-D 30108163 positive; radiation esophagitis 33580845 negative/futility; radiation enteritis 23471208 negative and possibly worse with glutamine; gut permeability meta-analysis 39397201 null overall with a high-dose subgroup signal). Sports-nutrition and healthy-aging oral trials (22048324, 25933498, 32411324, 32729784, 32992440, 33809996) are mostly small, mechanistic/biomarker-outcome studies with mixed or null results on hard endpoints. A substantial share of kept records are combination products (HMB/arginine/glutamine 'Juven'-type formulas, cystine+glutamine, arginine+glutamine+fish oil, alanyl-glutamine dipeptide, alkaline-water+glutamine) flagged related_form_differs -- these should not be read as evidence for isolated L-glutamine. Reviewers should weight the small set of clean, single-ingredient, placebo-controlled oral RCTs (30021096, 30108163, 10701731, 33580845, 23471208, 26709241, 28421779) most heavily for a single-ingredient label claim, and note that two of these single-ingredient trials (23471208, and secondary AEs in 30021096) point toward possible harm/no-benefit signals rather than uniformly positive evidence.
